ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the regular pentagon $ABCDE$, connect $AD$. What is the measure of $\angle 1$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the polygon interior angle sum theorem, we can deduce that the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon is $(5-2)\times 180^\circ=540^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AED=540^\circ\div 5=108^\circ$,\\
$\because$ in a regular pentagon $AE=DE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle 1=\angle EDA=\left(180^\circ-108^\circ\right)\div 2=\boxed{36^\circ}$

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: ABCDE is drawn as a pentagon with diagonal AD connected, and angle 1 is the angle at A between AD and AE, i.e. ∠DAE. From the text, use that ABCDE is a regular pentagon, so every interior angle is equal and all sides are equal. Compute each interior angle as ((5−2)×180°)/5 = 108°. In triangle AED, sides AE and DE are two sides of the regular pentagon, so AE = DE; hence triangle AED is isosceles with vertex angle ∠AED = 108°. Therefore the two base angles ∠DAE and ∠ADE are equal, each (180°−108°)/2 = 36°. Thus angle 1 is 36°.
